pinned-design.why-this-is-not-just-adding-:want: Confirmed by replay: freeze-prediction needs vector-or-coapply precedence, a declared horizon, and a normalized q0 with set-valued states. M-f11 currently declares no :horizon-steps (a source-declared T is mandatory — cascade_problems.clj:362-372 refuses :horizon-not-declared), and its sibling declared want :hole/h9ab212b3281d is already checked true at HEAD, which would refuse :selected-want-not-false-before for the whole receipt.

unresolved-semantic-decisions: D1 action identity: threading declaration-derived :want/:observation-locators onto the compiled selected action changes its digest (occurrence identity, trial configuration, dedup key). Enrich at construct-selected-action (identity changes, single producer) vs. pass an enriched view only to the accounting call sites (5918/7769) and accept that two digests of 'the action' exist. The first is cleaner; it is a decision because it invalidates identity continuity for in-flight runs.

D2 who mints the compiled route's prediction: extend freeze-prediction's own minter with the compiled shape (guard widening, above) — one schema, one producer — versus a new sibling producer. Recommendation: extend the existing minter; the record schema :wm/token-outcome-prediction-v1 already fits.

D3 horizon for compiled targets: declarations must carry :horizon-steps (T-repair does; M-f11, M-wm-08, M-aif do not — their effect predictions are currently unbuildable). Decision: require the declaration (fail-fast :horizon-not-declared at selection) versus deriving T from the compiled cascade length. Requiring the declaration preserves 'typed, never defaulted' (R13).

D4 stale declarations: a declaration whose declared wants include already-observed tokens (M-f11's h9ab212) can never verify end-to-end. Decision: declaration maintenance rule — when a want is observed true, the source's want list is narrowed (legitimate maintenance, distinct from retroactive completion).

D5 whether the compiled route's certificate should carry the token-belief-stage at compilation time (outer-policy contract change) instead of the runner computing it at selection-cell time. Runner-side keeps the outer-policy compilation contract unchanged.
